includes.description: Additional model sources to fetch and merge. Each must use this same format

propertyNames.description: Public model specifier. Unique, and carries the engine, e.g. gemma-4-27b-vllm

name.description: Display name of the model. Intended to be easily human readable

description.description: Multi-paragraph description: purpose, strengths, limitations. Shown when choosing between models, so a one-line label is not enough

url.description: External documentation url, for curious users that want to know more

anyOf.description: Identifier of a well-known license, expanded by the server into the full object

id.description: SPDX identifier, when this is a standard license. Display only

url.description: Link to the license text. For an unstated license, link the page a user should check instead

use.description: How far the license restricts using this model. `open` places no meaningful limit on use (Apache-2.0, MIT, CC-BY). `conditional` allows commercial use within bounds: revenue or user thresholds, acceptable-use policies, naming requirements. `non-commercial` forbids commercial use. `unknown` means the publisher states no terms, or terms this version does not recognise. This describes freedom to use, not obligations on redistribution, so copyleft licenses are `open`.

summary.description: One or two sentences telling a user what they may and may not do with this model. Required unless the license is open

license.description: License terms, as a well-known identifier or a full object. Governs what types of usage are permissible, if not all

createdAt.description: Date the model was published by its creator, as YYYY-MM-DD. Recency says a lot about capability, so it is shown wherever models are compared

registeredAt.description: Date this entry was added to the catalog, as YYYY-MM-DD. Entries added recently are flagged as new in the dashboard

engine.description: Inference engine this entry runs on

engineSpecifier.description: Identifier the engine itself uses. A HuggingFace model id for vLLM, a tag for Ollama

sizing.description: What this variant costs to run: how much VRAM it occupies, how much cache a token of context needs, and how far its context reaches

weightGb.description: Memory consumed by this variant's weights, in GB, wherever the engine keeps them

activeWeightGb.description: Weights read per token by a mixture-of-experts variant, in GB. Present exactly when the model is a mixture of experts, so it must be set for every one: it decides the concurrency knee and, when the model spans nodes, the extra collective communicator its experts need. Absent means dense, where every weight participates. Capacity still needs the full weight

hostWeightGb.description: Part of weightGb this entry's engine keeps in host memory instead of on the GPU, in GB, for example n-gram embedding tables. 0 when every weight is on the GPU. Stating it, 0 included, marks the entry as checked across nodes: without it the entry is placed on one node only, where it counts as 0

nonLayerWeightGb.description: Part of weightGb outside the decoder layer stack, in GB: input embedding, output head, vision and audio encoders. These sit on the first or last stage when the model is split by layers

layers.description: Decoder layers in the layer stack, num_hidden_layers in config.json, without speculative draft layers

attentionLayers.description: Layers that cache keys and values per token, including a speculative draft layer this entry enables. kvBytesPerToken is spread over these, which the engine pages per layer

stateLayers.description: Layers holding a fixed recurrent state per request, such as Mamba or gated deltanet layers. stateBytesPerSequence is spread over these. Absent for pure attention models

weightBits.description: Nominal bits per stored parameter, e.g. 16 for fp16 or 4 for AWQ. Never an exact average: every method leaves parts of the network wider than its headline width, commonly attention projections, embeddings and norms. Dividing weightGb by it yields a parameter count good enough to estimate throughput from, and good for nothing that needs the real one

minKvCacheGb.description: Minimum KV-cache allocation in decimal GB. Optional once kvBytesPerToken is stated, because the floor then follows from it: one request at full context in whole 16-token blocks plus the block the engine keeps in reserve, and for a hybrid model its per-sequence state. Author it only to demand more than that floor, and expect the server to log any entry whose figure disagrees with the derived one by more than a factor of two

kvBytesPerToken.description: KV cache one token of context consumes, in bytes, i.e. 2 * num_hidden_layers * num_key_value_heads * head_dim * dtype_bytes. How many requests a deployment can serve at once follows from this and the cache it was given, so it is the figure concurrency is computed from

maxContextLength.description: Maximum supported context window in tokens

attentionWindow.description: Sliding-window attention span in tokens, for models that have one. KV per request stops growing past this point, so a windowed model needs far less cache at long context than kvBytesPerToken alone suggests

stateBytesPerSequence.description: Recurrent state one concurrent request consumes, in bytes, for hybrid architectures whose layers are not all attention, such as Mamba or gated deltanet. Unlike kvBytesPerToken this does not grow with context: it is a fixed cost per request in flight. Present only for hybrid models, and vLLM refuses to start when its per-sequence state does not fit, so a concurrency cap that ignores it can be one the engine rejects

attentionHeads.description: Attention heads per layer of the language model, num_attention_heads in config.json

kvHeads.description: Key/value heads per layer of the language model, num_key_value_heads in config.json. Equal to attentionHeads without grouped-query attention, fewer with it

overheadGb.description: Deprecated and no longer read. The engine's own memory depends on how a deployment is split, not on the model, so it comes from the engine profile for the layout

mlaAttention.description: Whether the model uses multi-head latent attention, as DeepSeek V2 and V3 do, caching one compressed latent per token instead of keys and values per head

type.description: Usage type, which determines API compatibility

family.description: Family of the model. May be unknown

variantOf.description: Specifier of the standard variant of this model, when this entry is a variant of it. The UI presents the group together while each variant stays separately deployable and keeps its own license, description and capacity. A variant may not itself have variants

tags.description: Capabilities this variant supports: tools, vision, custom_code

unlisted.description: Keeps the entry out of the model picker without making it unusable. Deployments referencing it keep working, and a user can still reach it deliberately

unlistedReason.description: Shown to anyone who unhides the entry. Leave unset when the model is simply old, and use it when the reason changes what a user should do

engineArgs.description: Extra CLI arguments appended to the engine's command line. Arrays are deeply flattened to support YAML anchors

requestParams.description: Allowlist of extra request-level parameters the gateway may forward, as dot-notation paths mapped to primitive types. All are optional at request time

engineVersions.description: What this model needs of the engine version, and what specific releases do. Nodes running a blocked release are passed over when placing the model

min.description: Oldest engine version that serves this model correctly. Establish it empirically: a version can load cleanly and still fail the first request

rules.description: What specific releases at or above the floor do. A model can carry these without having a known floor

range.description: The releases this rule is about, as a single version or a range

effect.description: What the rule says about them. `blocked` keeps the model off nodes running one

reason.description: Why, in a sentence an operator can act on. For a block, what goes wrong and which release fixes it where that is known

platforms.description: GPU vendor requirement. Absent means any platform

placement.description: How an installation of this entry may be placed and split

limits.description: Restrictions on how an installation may be split that follow from no other field

max.description: Most machines one installation may span

reason.description: Why, in a sentence shown to someone choosing where to deploy

engineRange.description: The engine releases this limit applies to, as a version range. Absent means every release

max.description: Most cards one installation may span, over all its machines

reason.description: Why, in a sentence shown to someone choosing where to deploy

engineRange.description: The engine releases this limit applies to, as a version range. Absent means every release

values.description: The only numbers of cards one installation may be split across

reason.description: Why, in a sentence shown to someone choosing where to deploy

engineRange.description: The engine releases this limit applies to, as a version range. Absent means every release

minXinityVersion.description: Minimum xinity-ai version required to use this entry. Older clients skip entries they are too old for

downloadFilter.description: Gitignore-style glob patterns appended to the daemon's default HuggingFace download filter. Patterns starting with `!` re-include, and the last matching rule wins. Arrays are deeply flattened to support YAML anchors. Example: ["*.gguf", "!consolidated.safetensors"]

custom.description: Provenance for fine tuned custom models
